_comment: Room names and descriptions for area/hyrule.are, read by scripts/build_hyrule_area.py.
overworld: keyed by manifest coordinate. dungeons: "L<level>:<coordinate>", and
"L<level>:cellar:<coordinate>" for the block-stair cellar under that room; the generator
prefixes dungeon names with "Level N: ". special: caves, shops and secrets.
Descriptions are one paragraph each; the generator wraps them at 75 columns.

A1.name: Southwest Meadow
A1.description: A wide meadow of tall grass and wildflowers fills the far southwest corner of the land, hemmed in by brown rock to the south and west. Bees drone among the blossoms, and a strange whirring like a spinning top rises and fades on the wind. It is a quiet, forgotten place, and the only path leads east.

B1.name: Woodland Rock Face
B1.description: Trees crowd against a wall of brown rock that marks the southern edge of the land, their roots clinging to every crack. One stretch of the rock face is fractured and crumbling, a web of fine cracks spreading from its center as if a sharp blast might open it. Paths lead north, east and west through the woods.

C1.name: Southern Woods
C1.description: Old trees stand in loose rows along the southern edge of the land, their branches meeting overhead in a leafy roof. The ground is churned by heavy, clawed feet and littered with snapped twigs and gnawed bones. Somewhere off among the trunks a twig cracks. Paths lead north, east and west.

D1.name: Path to the Manji
D1.description: A narrow trail winds east through the woods toward a ring of trees that grow in an oddly regular pattern, too neat to be natural. The birdsong fades and the air grows cooler and quieter the farther east the path goes. Other trails branch away north and west into the deeper forest.

E1.name: Grove of the Manji
E1.description: A ring of tall trees encloses a hushed clearing, and at its center a dark stone entrance is carved in the shape of a turning, four-armed cross. Cold air breathes out of the doorway, smelling of moss, damp stone and something older. Rocks wall in the clearing on the south and east, and the only way out is west.

F1.name: Sandy Glade
F1.description: A clearing of loose, pale sand opens among the trees, oddly bare where the forest should be. The sand is rippled and pocked with small round burrow holes, and every so often it seems to stir on its own. Overhead something whirrs and spins in the air. Paths lead north into the woods and east toward the hills.

G1.name: Crags West of the Start
G1.description: Brown rock juts up in jagged ridges just west of a quiet green field, the ground between them dented where long-legged things have landed hard. One rock face looks cracked and weak, as if a good blast might open a way into it. Paths lead north, east toward the hills, and west into the woods.

H1.name: The First Quest Begins
H1.description: A small green field lies at the foot of rocky brown hills, quiet and sunny, the grass trampled into a faint path. In the cliff face to the north a dark cave mouth opens, and from within flickers the warm glow of twin fires. The wider world is no place to wander alone and empty-handed. Paths lead north, east and west.

I1.name: Meadow East of the Cave
I1.description: Open grassland stretches east from the starting hills, dotted with small boulders and clumps of bushes. Pebbles lie strewn across the grass as though spat from somewhere. One bush beside the rocks is dry and brittle, its leaves curling brown, plainly ready to burn. Paths lead north, east and west.

J1.name: Stone Field
J1.description: A field of jumbled grey and brown boulders sprawls across the southern edge of the land, the grass growing in tufts between them. One great stone sits loose in its bed, with fresh-turned earth around its base, as if a strong enough arm could shift it aside. The field opens east and west.

K1.name: Rocky Southern Ridge
K1.description: A rocky ridge runs along the southern edge of the land, brown stone breaking through thin, wind-flattened grass. The ground is scuffed with odd paired footprints that appear and vanish again several paces on, as if whatever made them leapt. Trails follow the ridge east and west.

L1.name: Southern Sands
L1.description: Sandy ground stretches along the southern edge of the land, rippled by the wind and pocked with burrow holes that open and close like breathing. To the south rises a rock wall, and one section of it is cracked and weak, as though a blast might open it. Paths lead north, east and west.

M1.name: Leever Dunes
M1.description: Low dunes of pale sand roll along the southern edge of the land, shifting and hissing whenever the wind picks up. Little whorls in the sand mark where something has burrowed down out of sight. A cracked face of rock rises at one side, as though a blast might open it. Paths lead east and west.

N1.name: Southern Shore Path
N1.description: A grassy path runs along the southern edge of the land, the low boom of the sea drifting from the east. Beside the path rises a wall of brown rock, and one section is cracked and crumbling, hollow-sounding when the wind moans past it. Small stones lie scattered in the grass. Paths lead east and west.

O1.name: Southeast Grassland
O1.description: Wide grassland sweeps toward the southeastern coast, the long grass bent flat by a constant wind that carries salt from the sea. Small round stones lie scattered about, some half buried as if spat with force. Gulls cry somewhere to the east. Paths lead east toward the shore and west across the grass.

P1.name: Southeast Coast
P1.description: The land ends at a rocky shore in the far southeastern corner of Hyrule, where grey waves crash and white spray drifts on the wind. Gulls wheel and cry overhead, and tide pools glimmer among the tumbled rocks. It is the very end of the world in two directions. Paths lead north along the coast and west inland.

A2.name: Western Meadow Edge
A2.description: Open meadow runs right up to the western edge of the land, where the grass stops at a sheer brown bluff. A strange rising whirr comes and goes on the wind, and deep, heavy hoofprints cut through the flowers as if something large and four-legged patrols here. Paths lead north toward the rocks and east into the woods.

B2.name: The Tangled Woods
B2.description: Dense trees crowd close on every side, their branches knotted overhead into a dim green roof. Paths wind away in all four directions between the trunks, and the only sounds are rustling leaves and the creak of old wood. Snapped spear-shafts lie half-buried in the leaf litter, dropped by whatever hunts these woods.

C2.name: Old Forest Clearing
C2.description: A hushed clearing opens among ancient oaks, their bark gnarled and split with age and their roots heaving up the soil. Fallen leaves lie ankle deep and smell of rain. At one edge a single bush has withered to a dry, papery brown, oddly lifeless beside the green. Trails wander away in every direction.

D2.name: Bramble Wood
D2.description: Thorny brambles crowd between the trunks, snagging cloth and skin alike, and the trail weaves a careful line through them. A bush beside the path has dried out completely, its leaves brittle and grey, and the ground behind it rings faintly hollow underfoot. Paths break away through the thorns in all four directions.

E2.name: The Lost Woods
E2.description: Every trunk here looks like every other, and the paths twist so strangely that a traveller can walk out one side of the grove and find the same trees waiting. A low rise above the trail holds the dark mouth of a cave, and a bitter smell of simmering herbs drifts from it. Near the path a lone bush stands dry and dead, brittle enough to catch from a single spark.

F2.name: Forest Stream
F2.description: A narrow stream threads through the trees, chattering over pebbles and pooling in quiet, fern-hung basins. Mossy stepping stones make for an easy crossing, though now and then the water swirls and bulges with no wind to stir it. Cool air rises off the current, and paths lead away in all four directions.

G2.name: Candle Shop Knoll
G2.description: A grassy knoll rises above the surrounding fields, crowned by a weathered outcrop of brown rock. A cave mouth in its side flickers with a soft yellow glow, and the warm smell of melted wax hangs about the entrance. Pebbles lie scattered over the slope as if hurled from somewhere. Paths lead east, west and south.

H2.name: Rock Wall Above the Start
H2.description: A wall of brown rock rises along the north side of a grassy field, its face scarred and cracked. One section looks weaker than the rest, as if a good blast might break it open. Trails lead east and west, and south toward a cave in the hills.

I2.name: Bush Row
I2.description: A tidy line of thick green bushes borders a sunny field, almost like a hedge someone once planted and forgot. One of them stands out from its neighbours, dry and brittle, its leaves browned and curled as though it would go up in flame in an instant. Worn paths cross the field to the north, south, east and west.

J2.name: River Bend
J2.description: A broad river swings through open country here, its water deep and green beneath an undercut, rocky bank. Reeds grow thick along the edge and dragonflies skim the shallows. Every so often the surface bulges and a wake slides away downstream. Dry ground leads north, east and west along the curve.

K2.name: Riverbank Thicket
K2.description: Dense bushes crowd the riverbank, their roots trailing into the slow brown water and their branches heavy with river mist. Among all that green, one bush stands dry and dead, its twigs grey and snapping in the breeze, as though waiting for a spark. Muddy paths lead north, east and west along the water.

L2.name: Shaded Grove
L2.description: Tall elms cast deep, cool shade over a quiet grove carpeted in soft moss. Birdsong falls silent here more often than it should. Near the path one bush has withered entirely, its brown leaves rattling like paper in the faintest breeze. The grove opens onto trails heading north, south, east and west.

M2.name: Dark Pine Stand
M2.description: Dark pines grow shoulder to shoulder, their needles thick and springy underfoot and their branches blotting out much of the sky. The still air smells of resin and old woodsmoke, and crude spear marks score several trunks at chest height. Narrow trails lead north, east and west between the trees.

N2.name: The Lion's Thicket
N2.description: A quiet clearing in the eastern forest is empty but for a single bush standing apart, dry and brittle and rooted in strangely flat, square-cut stone. Cold air seems to seep up from beneath its roots, carrying a smell of old masonry and deep places. Paths lead north, east and west through the trees.

O2.name: Eastern Wood Path
O2.description: A narrow trail runs east and west through a light, airy wood, sunlight dappling the ground between slender birches. Small round stones lie scattered along the track, some of them half buried as if they struck with force. From the east comes the steady hush of waves and a faint tang of salt on the breeze.

P2.name: Coastal Shop Cave
P2.description: Grassy bluffs overlook the eastern sea, where long grey waves break white on the rocks below. In a rocky bank set back from the cliff edge a cave mouth opens, and a sharp whiff of black powder drifts out to mingle with the salt air. The coast path runs north and south, and a track heads inland to the west.

A3.name: Western Crags
A3.description: Brown boulders and jagged rock spurs crowd the western edge of the world, and deep claw marks score the stone. Scattered bones bleach in the sun. To the north a channel of dark water cuts off the way, while a rough path winds south between the rocks.

B3.name: Deepwood Corner
B3.description: Old trees grow so close here that their canopy blots out the sky, leaving the forest floor in green gloom. Paths of trampled earth wind east and south between the trunks, and one bush near the trail is dry and brittle, its leaves brown and curling.

C3.name: Lost Woods Crossing
C3.description: The forest closes in on all sides, every trunk looking much like the next, and paths wander off in all four directions. Owls call in the shadows, and the moss grows on whichever side of the trees it pleases. To the north the trees begin to thin around a still clearing.

D3.name: The Fairy Path
D3.description: A narrow, mossy trail winds between the trees, and here and there a faint glimmer of light seems to dance ahead to the north. The rest of the woods is dim and muffled, its leaves trodden flat by heavy feet. Paths lead off in every direction.

E3.name: Forest River Ford
E3.description: A swift river splashes over a stony ford in the middle of the woods, cold and clear. The banks are slick with mud and covered in wet prints, and a sudden ripple now and then betrays something lurking beneath the surface. Paths lead on in all four directions.

F3.name: Shore Below the Snake
F3.description: The forest gives way to Lake Hylia's western waters, which glitter under an open sky. A small island rises a short distance to the north, and a dark serpent-shaped doorway can just be glimpsed on it across a narrow channel of water. Paths lead east, west and south along the shore.

G3.name: Lake Hylia, Southwest Bank
G3.description: Grassy banks slope down to the water's edge, where cattails sway and dragonflies hover. Out on the lake something breaks the surface and sinks again. A single dry bush grows near the path, ready to catch the slightest spark. Trails lead north, east and west.

H3.name: Lakeside Meadow
H3.description: A pleasant open meadow stretches out beneath the sky, the grass short and green and dotted with wildflowers. Small stones lie scattered about as though spat from somewhere, and the sound of lapping water drifts from the lake to the north. The meadow runs on east and west.

I3.name: Crossroads South of the Lake
I3.description: Two worn dirt roads cross in the middle of open green country. To the north the ground slopes down toward the sandy shore of Lake Hylia, and the smell of water hangs in the air. The roads lead off in all four directions across the grass.

J3.name: Flower Field
J3.description: A wide field of tall grass and bright flowers sways in the wind, humming with bees. Overhead there is a strange whirring sound, like something spinning in the air. The field is open on every side, with paths heading north, south, east and west.

K3.name: Rolling Green Downs
K3.description: Gentle green hills roll away beneath a broad sky, broken only by a few low rocks and scrubby bushes. The grass is pocked with small craters where stones have struck it hard. Paths lead east, west and south over the hills.

L3.name: Eastwood Glade
L3.description: A sunny glade sits in a ring of tall trees, the ground churned by heavy, clawed feet. Broken spear shafts lie in the long grass. One bush at the edge of the glade is as dry as old straw. Ways lead out in every direction.

M3.name: Pinewood Rise
M3.description: Tall pines climb a gentle slope, their needles thick and soft underfoot and their sap sharp in the air. Muddy tracks of something large and dog-headed criss-cross the trail. Paths lead east, west and south through the trees.

N3.name: Moblin Hollow
N3.description: A shallow hollow among the trees is strewn with trampled grass, chewed bones and the ashes of a cold campfire. The forest is noisy with snapping twigs and distant grunts. Paths climb out of the hollow in all four directions.

O3.name: Candlemaker's Dead End
O3.description: The forest trail runs out in a small hollow walled in by trees and a shoulder of grey rock. In the rock face a low cave mouth glows with a warm, steady flicker, and the smell of tallow and wick smoke drifts out on the still air. Beyond the hollow the woods are too thick to pass, so the only way back is west.

P3.name: The Coast's Lonely Ledge
P3.description: Rough grass runs down to the eastern shore, where the sea washes against tumbled rocks. Just offshore a small flat ledge of stone sits alone above the waves, separated from the land by a narrow strip of water. The coast path leads north and south.

A4.name: The Graveyard's Southern Fence
A4.description: Weathered headstones lean in crooked rows behind a low, crumbling wall, their names long since rubbed away by wind and rain. The grass grows thin and grey here and a cold mist clings to the ground. To the south the land drops to a band of dark water with a small stone landing, and the open country runs on to the east.

B4.name: Hollow of Headstones
B4.description: A sunken hollow of cracked gravestones sits under a sky that never quite seems to brighten. Crows' feathers and old wilted flowers litter the bare earth between the graves, and the air smells of damp soil. The burial ground climbs away northward, while a worn path slips out between the stones to the west.

C4.name: The Still Pond
C4.description: A ring of tall dark trees closes in around a round, perfectly still pond, its surface black and glassy. Smooth carved stones edge the water as though something was built beneath it long ago, and no breeze ever seems to touch the surface. Old folk say a certain tune can stir even sleeping water. The only way out is the forest track to the south.

D4.name: Fairy Pond of the Woods
D4.description: The forest opens onto a bright, clear pool fed by a quiet spring, its banks soft with moss and tiny white flowers. Motes of light drift and spin over the water, and the air feels warm and restful, as if weariness itself drains away here. A narrow track leads back south into the trees.

E4.name: Riverside Cave
E4.description: A swift green river cuts through the woods here, its banks lined with reeds and smooth grey stones. Across a stretch of grass a low cave mouth is set into a rocky bank, and the faint whiff of black powder drifts from inside. Trails follow the river north and south.

F4.name: Isle of the Snake
F4.description: A small green island rises out of the lake, ringed on every side by cold, lapping water. At its heart a dark stone entrance is carved in the coiled shape of a serpent, its doorway breathing out damp air. Across a narrow gap of water to the south lies the lakeshore, too wide to jump but narrow enough to bridge.

G4.name: Lake Hylia, Western Reeds
G4.description: Tall reeds rustle along the western edge of Lake Hylia, and the water slaps gently against a muddy bank. A lone, scraggly bush stands somewhat apart from the rest, dry and brittle as tinder. The shoreline curves away east, and a path climbs south through the grass.

H4.name: Lake Hylia, South Shore
H4.description: Broad blue water stretches north as far as the eye can see, sparkling under an open sky, its far shore lost in haze. Ripples spread from somewhere out in the deep. Near the bank a single dense bush grows by itself, dry and crackling in the sun. The shore runs on east and west.

I4.name: Lake Hylia Sand Bar
I4.description: A pale sand bar runs along the lake's edge, the sand rippled and pocked with odd little burrow holes. The water laps in long slow waves, and a lonely bush stands at the edge of the grass, brittle and brown. Paths lead north along the water, south toward the fields and west along the shore.

J4.name: Boulder Meadow
J4.description: Rolling green meadow is broken by heavy grey boulders that lie half sunk in the turf. One sits a little apart from the others, as if it had been rolled there by some great hand and might be rolled away again by a strong enough one. Trails lead off to the north, east and south.

K4.name: Craggy Rise
K4.description: Brown rock juts up through the grass in jagged ridges, and loose stones skitter down the slopes at every gust. The soil is scuffed with the prints of long-legged hopping things. Tucked under one ledge is a dark cave mouth that smells faintly of black powder. Paths run north, east and west.

L4.name: Eastern Thicket
L4.description: Dense trees crowd together here, their roots knotting across a narrow trail littered with snapped arrows and gnawed bones. One bush near the path looks unusually dry, its leaves curled and ready to catch the smallest spark. The thicket opens to the north, the south and the west.

M4.name: The Eastern Dock
M4.description: A weathered wooden dock juts out from the grassy bank over open water, its planks bleached grey and its posts green with weed. Water stretches away northward toward hazy islands, too far to swim. Behind the dock the meadow rolls off to the east.

N4.name: Wooded Crossroads
N4.description: Four forest paths meet in a small trampled clearing ringed by stout trees. Broken spearheads and torn bits of hide lie in the leaf litter. A single bush at the clearing's edge has dried out completely, its twigs as brittle as kindling. Ways lead off in every direction.

O4.name: Armos Sentinel Grove
O4.description: Stone knight statues stand in silent rows among the trees, shields raised and faces worn smooth by the years. They seem to watch the path, and one stands slightly out of line with the others, as if it had moved. The grove is a dead end, with the only way out leading back west.

P4.name: Eastern Cliffs
P4.description: The land ends abruptly at a line of rocky cliffs above the sea, and salt spray drifts up on a cool wind. Gulls wheel and cry overhead while waves boom against the rocks far below. A grassy track runs along the clifftop to the north and south.

A5.name: The Graveyard, Lower Rows
A5.description: The southern rows of the graveyard are crowded with weathered headstones, their names long worn away. Dead grass crackles underfoot, and a cold mist clings to the ground between the graves. The paths lead north into the older graves and east toward the living lands.

B5.name: The Graveyard Gate
B5.description: Here the graves thin out toward the edge of the burial ground, where a gap in the boundary lets travellers pass. The headstones nearest the gate lean outward as if to see who comes and goes. The mist gathers thickest by the gap, and the air smells of cold earth.

C5.name: Ghost Hill
C5.description: A low grassy hill overlooks the graveyard to the west, its slopes dotted with wildflowers and scarred by heavy hoofprints. The air here is warmer than among the graves. A narrow cleft runs north toward the highlands, and the way continues east and west.

D5.name: The Cracked Bluff
D5.description: A tall bluff of brown rock stands at the edge of the highlands, its face stained by old water. Near its base the stone is cracked and flaking, and a faint herbal scent drifts out of the gaps. A narrow cleft leads north, and the land opens to the west.

E5.name: The Silent Sentinels
E5.description: A cluster of stone soldiers stands guard on a patch of sandy ground, their spears raised in perpetual salute. The sand around them is restless and churns in small spirals. One statue stands a little apart from the others, its base scuffed as if it had shifted. The only way out leads south.

F5.name: The Quiet Glade
F5.description: Tall trees ring a peaceful glade of soft grass, and the light falls in gentle patches through their leaves. Birdsong drifts from the branches. A narrow gully leads north toward the higher country, and the glade opens to the east.

G5.name: The Sheltered Hollow
G5.description: A hollow is tucked between low hills, sheltered from the wind and quiet. Green grass grows thick and undisturbed, and a few trees stand at its edges. Paths lead north and west, and the stillness here feels like a held breath.

H5.name: The Eagle's Gate
H5.description: On a spit of green land cut off by the river, a stone entrance stands in a rocky outcrop, its lintel carved with the spread wings of an eagle. Cool, musty air drifts from the darkness within. The river runs wide to the east, where a wooden dock waits for anyone with a way to cross.

I5.name: The River Landing
I5.description: The river widens here, and a sturdy wooden dock juts out from the bank into the current. Across the water to the west a green shore waits, unreachable on foot. Grass grows thick along the bank, and the land opens to the north and south.

J5.name: The Fairy Fountain, North
J5.description: A clear pool lies in a ring of soft grass, its surface glittering with tiny motes of light. The water is perfectly still and smells of rain and flowers, and a warmth seems to rise from it that eases every ache. A path leads away to the south.

K5.name: The Peahat Fields
K5.description: Wide fields of grass and wildflowers stretch out under an open sky. Flowers spin and whirl as though caught in some strange wind, and patches of sand show through the turf here and there. Paths lead off to the north, east and south.

L5.name: The Blowing Sands
L5.description: Sand drifts across this stretch of the field in long, low ridges, burying the grass in places. Small mounds appear and vanish in the sand, as if something stirred beneath it, and the wind lifts fine grit that stings the eyes. The way leads north, south and west.

M5.name: The Moon Gate
M5.description: A stone entrance stands near the water's edge, its doorway crowned with a carved crescent moon. Damp air drifts from inside, smelling of stone and old water. The lake's edge cuts off the south, where a wooden dock juts into the water.

N5.name: The Armos Shore
N5.description: A row of stone soldiers stands on a grassy rise above the lake, their spears raised. One statue stands slightly apart from the others, its base scuffed and cracked as if it had moved. Paths lead north and south along the shore, and the air smells of water and grass.

O5.name: The Octorok Banks
O5.description: The grassy bank slopes gently to the water's edge, scattered with spat stones and small rocks. The lake glitters to the south and east, and reeds rustle wherever the water meets the grass. A path leads east along the shore and north toward the cliffs.

P5.name: Lake Hylia, Eastern Dock
P5.description: A wooden dock reaches out into Lake Hylia from the eastern shore, and across the water a small green island sits alone. The water is deep and dark near the dock, and bubbles rise from beneath it now and then. The shore continues south and west.

A6.name: The Old Graveyard
A6.description: Row upon row of grey headstones stand in the cold earth, many tilted and half sunk. The grass between them is withered, and a chill hangs in the air that the sun cannot burn off. Thin mist curls around the stones, and the silence feels like it is listening.

B6.name: The Master Sword Grave
B6.description: The graveyard reaches its oldest corner here, where the headstones are tallest and most worn. One grave sits a little apart, its stone slightly askew on a slab that looks as though it could be shifted. The cold is deepest near it, and the dead seem restless all around.

C6.name: The Dragon's Gate
C6.description: Bare highland rock surrounds a dark entrance carved into a low outcrop, its mouth framed by stone shaped like the coiled body of a dragon. Hot, stale air breathes out of it. Lynel tracks and scorch marks cover the ground, and a narrow gap leads away to the south.

D6.name: The Western Warp Stone
D6.description: A lonely boulder sits in a ring of trampled grass, heavier and squarer than the stones around it. The earth at its base is scraped, as if something beneath had been uncovered and covered again. Deep hoofprints circle the place, and a narrow cleft drops away to the south.

E6.name: The Armos Gallery
E6.description: A row of carved stone soldiers stands at attention across the highland, each holding a spear, their blank eyes fixed on the horizon. They look patient and very old. One of them stands slightly off true from the others. A narrow cleft to the north leads toward the mountain.

F6.name: The Bomb Merchant's Cave
F6.description: Flowers carpet this open field, and a cave mouth yawns in a low rock face at its western side. A smell of black powder and burnt fuses lingers at the entrance. Narrow gullies cut the land to north and south, and the wind sends ripples across the grass.

G6.name: The Meadow Bluff
G6.description: A grassy meadow runs up against a weathered bluff, bright with wildflowers that sway and whirl in the breeze. Part of the bluff's face is fractured and loose, with a faint draught slipping through the cracks. The meadow opens to the east and slopes down to the south.

H6.name: Foot of Death Mountain
H6.description: Here the green fields meet the brown flanks of Death Mountain, and a path climbs northward into the boulders. Flowers grow thick along the trail. In a rocky outcrop beside the path, one section is cracked and crumbling, and a bitter herbal scent drifts from somewhere behind it.

I6.name: The Withered Thicket
I6.description: Open grassland is broken here by clusters of dry, scrubby bushes. One bush stands alone, its branches brittle and dead, and it looks as if a single spark would set it ablaze. Blackened twigs and old ash lie scattered about it, and the field opens in every direction but north.

J6.name: The Sandy Flats
J6.description: The grass gives way to a stretch of pale, shifting sand, warm underfoot and strangely restless. Small mounds rise and sink across it as though something burrowed just beneath the surface. The flats run east and west, and the air shimmers with heat.

K6.name: The Dune Strip
K6.description: A long strip of dunes runs between the green fields and the mountains, the sand rippled into fine waves by the wind. Spiral burrow marks appear and fade across it. The way leads east, west and south, and the brown peaks loom to the north.

L6.name: Below the Lost Hills
L6.description: Sand and scrub mingle at the foot of the rolling hills to the north, where a narrow cleft climbs toward them. The ground here is soft and pocked with burrow holes. Paths lead off in every direction, and the hills above seem to shift whenever you look away.

M6.name: Lake Hylia, North Cliffs
M6.description: Brown cliffs rise from the northern edge of Lake Hylia, and the blue water glints below. The rock is dented by springing marks, and one part of the cliff face is split with deep cracks, a cool draught breathing through them. A gap in the rock leads north toward the mountains.

N6.name: Lake Hylia, North Shore
N6.description: Green grass runs down to the lake's northern shore, where small waves lap at a strip of pebbles. Spat stones lie scattered on the turf. A low rock face at the back of the shore is cracked through in one place, and a narrow gap leads north into the mountains.

O6.name: Lake Hylia, Northeast Shore
O6.description: The shore curves here around a broad sweep of Lake Hylia, the water deep and dark close to the bank. Bubbles rise now and then from beneath the surface. Tufts of grass fringe the rocks, and the shoreline continues west and south.

P6.name: The Lonely Isle
P6.description: A small island sits alone in the eastern waters of Lake Hylia, a patch of green grass ringed by blue. Waves slap gently at its edges. No path leads here except across the water, and the only way back is by a little dock on the southern side, facing the far shore.

A7.name: The Western Gorge
A7.description: Steep brown walls box in this gorge at the western edge of the mountains, and the wind funnels through with a low howl. Hoofprints cross and recross the floor. In one wall a crack spreads like a spider's web, and the stone around it rings faintly hollow. Northward, a deep crevice splits the rock.

B7.name: The Windswept Shelf
B7.description: A flat shelf of rock juts out from the mountainside, scoured clean by constant wind. A few tough flowers grow in the lee of the boulders, their petals torn ragged. A crevice runs along the northern edge, and the only easy way off the shelf leads west.

C7.name: The Shieldmaker's Bluff
C7.description: A blunt bluff of brown stone rises from the slope, its face streaked with mineral stains. Low down, a section of it is cracked and loose, and the faint ring of a hammer on metal seems to come from somewhere inside. The trail leads east, and a narrow gap opens in the rock to the north.

D7.name: Broken Stone Terrace
D7.description: Terraces of broken stone step down the mountainside like a ruined stair. Lynel tracks, deep and wide, scar the dust between them. At the back of one terrace the cliff is fissured and weak, as if hiding a hollow behind it. A crevice to the north separates this place from the heights.

E7.name: The Crumbling Scarp
E7.description: The scarp here is old and tired, its brown face slumping into heaps of rubble. One stretch looks ready to give way altogether, its cracks deep enough to whistle in the wind. Scorch marks blacken the boulders, and a narrow gully drops away to the south toward greener land.

F7.name: Highland Overlook
F7.description: The mountain pauses here in a high meadow of thin grass and wildflowers, ringed by brown boulders. From its edge the whole of the western highlands spreads below. The wind carries the scent of the lowlands up the slope, and narrow clefts break the ground to north and south.

G7.name: The Rumbling Gully
G7.description: A gully runs east and west beneath an unstable cliff, and every few moments a rock tumbles from above and bounds across it. Gravel crunches underfoot. One section of the gully wall is split with fresh cracks, and a faint clink, like coins being counted, seems to echo behind it.

H7.name: The Lost Hills
H7.description: Brown hills rise and fall here, each fold of ground so like the last that the eye loses its place among them. The trail climbs north toward the high peaks between banks of loose scree, and paths wander off east and west along the slope. Those who know the mountain say the only way through is to keep climbing north and never turn aside.

I7.name: The Boulder Run
I7.description: Loose rocks careen down the mountainside and across this stretch of trail, leaving it littered with splinters of stone. The cliffs on either side are scarred where boulders have struck them. Dust hangs in the air and the clatter never fully stops.

J7.name: Rolling Stone Ravine
J7.description: A shallow ravine runs east and west between walls of crumbling brown rock. Stones break free from the rim and roll down the slope in short, bouncing bursts. Gouges in the ravine floor mark their favourite paths, and the air tastes of dust.

K7.name: The Springing Hills
K7.description: Rolling brown hills begin here, each one shaped so much like the last that the eye loses its place among them. The ground is dented with springing marks, as though something leapt from hilltop to hilltop. To the north a narrow cleft divides the hills from the high country.

L7.name: Hills Below the Basin
L7.description: Brown hills rise and fall in every direction here, scored by narrow crevices that cut the ground to the north and south. The wind moans through the gaps between them like distant laughter, and loose stones skitter down the slopes at every gust. Paths wind east and west along the ridgelines.

M7.name: Lone Armos Ridge
M7.description: A single weathered stone soldier stands guard on this narrow ridge, its carved face worn smooth by the wind. Brown rock falls away on both sides. Gaps in the ridge open to the north and south, and the ground around the statue is oddly scuffed, as if it sometimes stepped off its post.

N7.name: The Heavy Boulder
N7.description: A small high meadow is ringed by boulders, and one of them sits a little apart from the rest, squarer and heavier, with a scraped track in the earth beside it as though it had once been moved. Flowers grow thick here and bob in the wind. Narrow clefts lead north and south.

O7.name: The Scarred Cliffs
O7.description: These cliffs are pocked and gouged, and one patch in particular is laced with cracks so deep that light seems to show between them. Springing marks dent the dusty ground. The way runs east and west along the base of the rock, and a crevice opens to the north.

P7.name: The Eastern Cliffs
P7.description: The mountains drop sharply to the east here, and a broad shelf of rock catches the morning sun. A cave mouth opens in the cliff, and from its shadow comes the faint rattle of something being shaken, then laughter. Wildflowers grow along the shelf, and a cleft splits the rock to the north.

A8.name: Death Mountain's Western Summit
A8.description: The world ends here in a wall of brown boulders, stacked shoulder to shoulder against a pale, empty sky. Thin wind whistles through the gaps and carries nothing but grit. To the south a narrow crevice splits the stone, too wide to step across and too deep to see the bottom of.

B8.name: Lynel Ridge
B8.description: A high ridge of rust-brown rock runs east and west, its ground churned by heavy hooves and dotted with scorched patches where something breathed fire. One stretch of the cliff face is webbed with fine cracks, as though the stone behind it were hollow. A deep cleft bars the way south.

C8.name: The High Boulder Pass
C8.description: Rounded boulders the size of huts crowd this pass, leaving a crooked lane of bare earth between them. The air is thin and cold, and every sound bounces back twice from the cliffs. Hoofprints and singed lichen mark the trail, and a sheer-sided crevice opens in the rock to the south.

D8.name: Rockfall Crest
D8.description: Loose scree pours down from the peaks above, and every so often a fresh stone comes bounding across the crest with a hollow clatter. The ground is pocked with craters from earlier falls. In the northern cliff one patch of rock looks oddly brittle, flaking at a touch, and a narrow gap cuts the slope to the south.

E8.name: The Medicine Woman's Ledge
E8.description: Walled in on three sides by brown crags, this quiet ledge opens only to the east. A dark cave mouth is set into the rock, its threshold swept clean, and a faint bitter smell of boiled herbs drifts out of it. The ground nearby is trampled by heavy hooves, and the wind moans over the rim.

F8.name: Spectacle Rock
F8.description: Two great round boulders stand side by side on the summit, joined by a low saddle of stone, like a giant's pair of spectacles left on the mountaintop. Sand has blown into drifts between them. Part of the rock wall here sounds hollow and is seamed with hairline cracks; the air near it is colder than it ought to be.

G8.name: East of Spectacle Rock
G8.description: A broad shelf of packed earth stretches between rows of brown boulders, the twin humps of Spectacle Rock just visible to the west. Wind-flattened weeds cling to the cracks, and a few hardy flowers nod in the gusts. Far below, the green of Hyrule spreads out like a quilt.

H8.name: The Summit Road
H8.description: A worn path threads east and west along the mountain's crown, hemmed in by tumbled boulders. One face of the cliff shows a dark crack running from top to bottom, as if a single blow might open it. To the south the trail stops at a narrow chasm with the mountain trail visible beyond.

I8.name: Avalanche Slope
I8.description: The mountain sheds itself constantly here. Rocks break loose from the heights and come bouncing down in long arcs, smashing into gravel on the boulders below. The path east and west is littered with shattered stone, and the dust never quite settles.

J8.name: Death Mountain's Dead End
J8.description: Boulders close in on every side but the west, forming a still, sheltered pocket at the top of the world. The silence is heavy after the clatter of the slopes. Nothing grows here but grey lichen, and the only marks in the dust are the wind's.

K8.name: The White Sword Falls
K8.description: A river spills over the lip of the mountain and drops in a roaring white curtain, filling the air with cold spray and rainbows. Beside the falls, at the very top of the climb, a cave mouth opens in the rock, half hidden by mist. Ripples in the pool below suggest something moves beneath the water.

L8.name: The Lizard's Gate
L8.description: Beyond the confusing folds of the Lost Hills the ground levels into a hidden basin of reddish sand. At its heart a squat entrance is cut into the stone, framed in a carved shape like a crouching lizard, its doorway black and cool. Dry wind hisses through the sand, and a crevice bars the way back south.

M8.name: The Candle Merchant's Hollow
M8.description: A dip among the high boulders shelters a cave mouth from the worst of the wind. A whiff of tallow and lamp smoke hangs at the entrance, and the dust before it is scuffed by many feet. Small craters show where something springs and lands, springs and lands, all across the hollow.

N8.name: Tektite Heights
N8.description: The rock here is pitted with shallow dents, as though something heavy had been bouncing across it for years. Brown cliffs rise to the north, and one section of them is cracked and crumbling, with a faint draught whispering out of the seams. A narrow gap divides the heights from the land to the south.

O8.name: Ledge of the Letter Cave
O8.description: A lonely ledge looks out over the eastern slopes, with a cave mouth gaping in the cliff behind it. Inside, a warm glow flickers, as though a pair of fires were kept burning against the cold. The wind is softer here, and the hush feels like a place where messages wait for the right hands.

P8.name: The Northeast Crag
P8.description: The far corner of the mountains ends in a sheer brown crag above the eastern wilds. A dark cave opens in its base, small and easily overlooked, with an air of secrets kept from everybody. Stubborn shrubs grow in the cracks, and a deep cleft to the south falls away into shadow.

L1:B1.name: West Guardroom
L1:B1.description: A plain square chamber of blue-grey flagstones, its corners furred with dust and spattered with bat droppings. Something leathery has left fine scratches along the high ledges, and a faint flutter echoes now and then from the ceiling. The only way out is the open doorway east, back toward the entry.

L1:C1.name: Eagle Gate
L1:C1.description: Cold teal stone rises on every side of this first chamber, the walls carved with rows of grim, staring faces. Daylight from the stair behind fades within a few paces, and the air smells of wet rock. Open doorways lead east and west, while the northern door is barred shut and fitted with a heavy iron keyhole.

L1:D1.name: East Bone Room
L1:D1.description: Bleached bone fragments lie scattered across the tiled floor of this chamber, and the air carries the dry, chalky smell of old marrow. Two squat stone blocks stand near the middle of the room like plinths waiting for statues. A single open doorway leads west to the entry.

L1:C2.name: Rattling Passage
L1:C2.description: A row of squat stone blocks runs across the middle of this chamber, dividing it into two narrow lanes. Bones have been kicked into the corners, and a faint rattle seems to linger after every sound. A locked door with a brass-ringed keyhole leads south, and an open arch leads north.

L1:B3.name: Shuttered West Room
L1:B3.description: A low-ceilinged chamber of chill teal stone, where bat droppings crust the tops of a few scattered blocks and a papery rustle drifts down from the dark. The air tastes of dust. A heavy iron shutter fills the eastern doorway, and the north door is locked, its keyhole ringed with rust.

L1:C3.name: Diamond-Tiled Crossing
L1:C3.description: Four ways meet in this broad chamber, its floor laid in worn diamond-patterned tiles. A heavy iron shutter is sunk into the western doorway, and open arches lead east and south. Part of the north wall is crazed with dark hairline fissures, as if a sharp blow might bring it down.

L1:D3.name: Bat Roost
L1:D3.description: The ceiling of this chamber vanishes into darkness, and the stale air is thick with the musk of roosting bats. Droppings crust the floor between low rows of raised blocks, and the walls whisper with the beat of unseen wings. An open doorway leads west, and a patch of the north wall is cracked and sounds hollow.

L1:A4.name: Hall of the Twin Fires
L1:A4.description: Two fires burn in stone braziers at the far end of this quiet chamber, throwing warm, steady light across the flagstones. Between them an old man stands as though he has always been there, murmuring that the eastmost peninsula is the secret. A heavy iron shutter seals the eastern doorway.

L1:B4.name: Slime-Slick Hall
L1:B4.description: The flagstones here are tacky with a faint glistening film, and small wet smears wander across them in no particular direction. The smell is sour, like spoiled broth. A locked door with a keyhole leads south, an open archway leads east, and a heavy iron shutter fills the western doorway.

L1:C4.name: Chamber of Pillars
L1:C4.description: Square stone blocks march across this large chamber in a rigid grid, leaving narrow lanes between them, and gelatinous smears gleam on the tiles. Open doorways lead north and west, a locked door with a keyhole bars the east, and the south wall is split by a dark web of cracks.

L1:D4.name: Scarred Hall
L1:D4.description: Curved gouges and scuff marks score the walls at shoulder height, as if something has been flung against them again and again and caught on the way back. A few stone blocks crouch near the corners. An open doorway leads east, a locked door leads west, and the south wall is fractured and weak.

L1:E4.name: Hall of Grasping Walls
L1:E4.description: The walls of this chamber seem to press closer than they should, and dark handprints smudge the stone high up near the ceiling. The air is still and watchful, and the shadows along the edges never quite sit right. An open doorway leads west, while the north door is locked fast, its keyhole worn bright.

L1:C5.name: Ossuary Hall
L1:C5.description: Old bones lie heaped in drifts against the walls of this dim chamber, and a pair of stone blocks squats near its center. The faint clatter of something settling never quite stops. An open arch leads south, and a locked door with an iron keyhole stands to the north.

L1:E5.name: Aquamentus's Lair
L1:E5.description: Scorch marks blacken the floor of this long chamber, fanning out from a great ledge of stone along the eastern wall. The air is hot and stinks of sulphur and charred bone, and shed green scales glint among the cinders. A locked door leads south, and a heavy iron shutter seals the way east.

L1:F5.name: Triforce Chamber
L1:F5.description: A small, hushed chamber of smooth teal stone, its floor framed by a border of carved blocks. A soft golden glow seems to hang in the air though nothing here burns, and the stone is warm to the touch. A heavy iron shutter leads west, back toward the dragon's lair.

L1:B6.name: Chamber of Blade Traps
L1:B6.description: Deep grooves run across the floor of this chamber from its corners, polished smooth by heavy blades that rest against the walls, ready to slide. A single stone block in the middle sits a little askew, its base scraped as though it has been shifted before. A locked door leads east.

L1:C6.name: Northern Guardroom
L1:C6.description: Curved scuff marks and dents pock the walls of this high northern chamber, and the floor is littered with chips of broken stone. Cold air drifts down from cracks in the vaulted ceiling. Locked doors with heavy keyholes stand to the south and to the west.

L1:cellar:B6.name: Bow Cellar
L1:cellar:B6.description: A narrow ladder drops from the stair into a long, shadowy basement of brick ledges and black gaps that fall away into nothing. The air is cool and smells of earth and old candle wax. A raised stone shelf waits at the far end of the ledges, and the ladder climbs back to the chamber above.

L2:B1.name: Crescent Gate
L2:B1.description: Pale blue stone surrounds this entrance hall, its walls carved with crescent moons worn soft by time. A chill draft spills down the stair behind, carrying the smell of the green hills outside. Open doorways lead north and east into the darker halls beyond.

L2:C1.name: Shed Skin Chamber
L2:C1.description: Papery snake skins lie curled in the corners of this blue-walled chamber, and thin sinuous tracks wind through the dust on the floor. Squat stone blocks frame the center of the room. An open doorway leads west to the entrance, and another leads north deeper into the dungeon.

L2:A2.name: Coiled Track Room
L2:A2.description: A dead-end chamber on the dungeon's western edge, its dusty floor scored by long looping drag marks. The air is musty and faintly reptilian, and a dry rasp seems to come and go along the walls. A heavy iron shutter seals the only doorway, to the east.

L2:B2.name: Blue Antechamber
L2:B2.description: Stone blocks stand in two short rows across this chamber, and the blue walls sweat a faint chill. Shed scales gleam between the floor tiles like flakes of mica. Open doorways lead east and south toward the entrance, while the western door is a heavy iron shutter.

L2:C2.name: Moonstone Crossroads
L2:C2.description: Wide and echoing, this chamber sits where several halls meet, its tiles worn into shallow paths by the passage of countless scaled bellies. Open doorways lead north, south and west, and the east door is locked, its keyhole set in a bronze plate shaped like a waning moon.

L2:D2.name: Dripping Chamber
L2:D2.description: Water beads on the ceiling of this eastern chamber and drips onto tiles filmed with faint jelly-like slime. Rows of blocks divide the floor into narrow aisles that smell of damp. A locked door with a keyhole leads west, and the north wall is threaded with fine cracks that look ready to give.

L2:C3.name: Gouged Hall
L2:C3.description: Curving gouges mark the walls of this chamber, and the floor is littered with chips of blue stone knocked loose by something hurled hard and often. Pairs of blocks flank the middle. An open doorway leads south, a locked door bars the east, and a heavy iron shutter fills the doorway north.

L2:D3.name: Cracked Eastern Room
L2:D3.description: A narrow eastern room whose walls are fractured top and bottom, the cracks wide enough to let a cold draft whisper through. Faint slime trails glisten across the floor and dry into crusts along the baseboards. A locked door leads west, while the north and south walls look thin and hollow.

L2:C4.name: Long Hall of the Moon
L2:C4.description: This chamber is part of the long north-south spine of the dungeon, its blue walls rising unbroken to a shadowed vault. Slither marks cross the dusty floor in lazy curves between the blocks. A heavy shutter seals the south, and open doorways lead north and east.

L2:D4.name: Eastern Hall of Cuts
L2:D4.description: Deep, curving cuts score the walls of this room, and a scatter of broken masonry lies near the center. The air smells of oiled leather and old dust, and a faint whirring echo seems to circle the ceiling. An open doorway leads west, while both the north and south walls are veined with cracks.

L2:C5.name: Silent Chamber
L2:C5.description: An empty, silent chamber of pale blue stone, its floor swept bare and its corners deep in shadow. Nothing stirs here, and every footstep rings loud off the walls and comes back a moment late. Open doorways lead north, south and east along the dungeon's long spine.

L2:D5.name: Trap-Grooved Room
L2:D5.description: Polished grooves cut across the floor of this cramped eastern room, running wall to wall where something heavy slides on its own. Bat droppings stain the upper ledges, and the air is stale. An open doorway leads west, and the north and south walls are both cracked and hollow-sounding.

L2:C6.name: Serpent Hall
L2:C6.description: Coiled tracks and shed skins cover the floor of this long chamber, and the air is warm and close with reptile musk. A double row of stone blocks runs down its middle like a colonnade. An open doorway leads south, a locked door bars the east, and a heavy shutter stands to the north.

L2:D6.name: Slime-Pooled Cell
L2:D6.description: Glistening smears of slime trail across this small chamber, pooling in the grout between the tiles and dripping from the lip of the blocks. The walls are close and clammy. An open doorway leads north, a locked door with a keyhole leads west, and the south wall is laced with fine cracks.

L2:C7.name: Smoke-Stained Antechamber
L2:C7.description: Gouged walls and scattered stone chips mark this chamber below the dungeon's northern end. A low rumble seems to come from beyond the north wall, and the air smells faintly of smoke and powder. Heavy shutters stand north and south, and the east wall is split by a web of cracks.

L2:D7.name: Northeast Hollow
L2:D7.description: A quiet dead-end chamber in the dungeon's northeast corner, its tiles slick with an oily film and its blocks beaded with damp. Water drips steadily from somewhere above. An open doorway leads south, and the west wall is fractured and loose, as if only old mortar holds it up.

L2:B8.name: Triforce Chamber
L2:B8.description: A small sanctum of quiet blue stone in the dungeon's far northwest, its floor framed by a border of raised blocks. A gentle golden light seems to hang in the air, and the hush here is deep and reverent after the smoke next door. An open doorway leads east, back to the lair.

L2:C8.name: Dodongo's Lair
L2:C8.description: A broad, low chamber that stinks of smoke and scorched rock, its floor pitted with blast craters and pressed by huge three-toed footprints. Blackened scraps of fuse lie among the rubble, and the walls are sooty to the ceiling. A heavy shutter seals the south door, and an open doorway leads west.

L3:C1.name: Ooze Chamber
L3:C1.description: Thick, glistening puddles of slime spread across this square chamber, and the stone is stained a sickly green where they have dried. A pair of blocks stands near the middle, crusted at their bases. Open doorways lead east to the entrance and north into the dungeon.

L3:D1.name: Manji Gate
L3:D1.description: Green-tinged stone closes around this entrance hall, its walls carved with angular hooked patterns that turn in on themselves like the dungeon's own crooked plan. Cool, damp air rises from deeper within, smelling of moss. The only doorway leads west.

L3:A2.name: Knight's Dead End
L3:A2.description: Heavy boot prints and the long scrape of armored feet mar the dust in this far western chamber. Stone blocks stand in a loose ring, and one sits slightly out of line with the rest, its edges scuffed as though it has been shoved. A heavy iron shutter seals the doorway north.

L3:C2.name: Streaked Hall
L3:C2.description: Long streaks of slime run down the walls of this hall, as if something heavy had tried to climb them and slid back down. The air is damp and smells of rot and wet stone, and the floor squelches in places. Open doorways lead north and south.

L3:A3.name: Armored Hall
L3:A3.description: Deep blade scratches line the walls of this western hall, and the floor is scuffed by heavy armored steps that pace back and forth. Squares of stone block lie in a checker pattern. An open doorway leads north, a locked door with a keyhole leads east, and a heavy shutter seals the south.

L3:B3.name: Hall of Blades
L3:B3.description: Smooth grooves cut along the walls of this chamber, worn deep by steel-edged traps that rest in all four corners. Bat droppings speckle the floor in the lanes between them, and the ceiling rustles. Open doorways lead north and east, and a locked door with a keyhole stands to the west.

L3:C3.name: Manji Crossing
L3:C3.description: This is the heart of the dungeon's crooked cross, a broad chamber where halls meet from every side. Green slime pools in the low places between the worn floor tiles. Open doorways lead north, south and west, and the east wall is split by deep cracks that look ready to crumble.

L3:D3.name: Eastern Slime Hall
L3:D3.description: Glistening sludge coats the floor of this chamber in thick, drying layers, and the smell of damp moss hangs heavy. A row of blocks lines the far wall. An open doorway leads north, a heavy iron shutter seals the east, and the west wall is fractured and sounds hollow when struck.

L3:E3.name: Chamber of Cold Flickers
L3:E3.description: A creeping chill hangs in this small chamber, and pale blue flickers seem to dance at the edge of sight before winking out. Bat droppings and shards of old bone lie across the stone. Heavy iron shutters seal both the north and the west doorways.

L3:A4.name: Haunted West Room
L3:A4.description: A dim chamber at the dungeon's western reach, where eerie flickers of light seem to wink in the corners and vanish when looked at directly. Bat droppings crust the ledges, and the air is cold and thin. Open doorways lead east and south.

L3:B4.name: Bat Gallery
L3:B4.description: The ceiling of this chamber is pocked with crevices where bats roost, and the floor beneath is stained with their droppings. Two blocks stand near the center, chipped by claws. Open doorways lead west and south, and a locked door with a keyhole bars the east.

L3:C4.name: Hall of Three Locks
L3:C4.description: Locked doors stand on three sides of this chamber, north, east and west, each with a heavy keyhole set in iron, and only the southern arch stands open. Slime smears glisten across the floor and dry to a green crust along the base of the walls.

L3:D4.name: Room of Sliding Blades
L3:D4.description: Four steel-edged traps rest in the corners of this chamber, and the floor between them is cut with straight, polished grooves. An open doorway leads south and a locked door leads west. The east wall is cracked from floor to ceiling, and a sweet, green smell seeps through the fissures.

L3:E4.name: Manhandla's Lair
L3:E4.description: Thick vines and torn, fleshy petals carpet this chamber, and the air is heavy with the cloying sweetness of some monstrous bloom. Long whip-marks and scorch spots score the floor in every direction. Heavy shutters seal the north and south doorways, and the west wall is cracked, its stones loose.

L3:C5.name: Blade Corridor
L3:C5.description: Twin grooves cut across this narrow chamber where heavy blades rest against the walls, poised to slide at the first footstep. The stone between them is scored with fresh, bright scratches. A locked door leads south, and a heavy iron shutter seals the doorway north.

L3:E5.name: Triforce Chamber
L3:E5.description: A quiet chamber of green stone above the lair, its floor framed by a border of raised blocks. A warm golden light lingers in the air, and the stone here is clean and untouched by slime or vine. A heavy iron shutter leads south, back into the overgrown lair.

L3:B6.name: Northwest Roost
L3:B6.description: Shadows crowd the high corners of this quiet chamber, and the musk of roosting bats hangs thick in the air. Droppings stain the tiles in long pale streaks, and wings stir faintly overhead. A heavy iron shutter seals the eastern doorway, the only way in or out.

L3:C6.name: Firelit Hall of Riddles
L3:C6.description: Two fires crackle in stone braziers at the north end of this chamber, casting warm amber light across the green stone. Between them an old man waits, asking every visitor whether they got the sword from the old man atop the waterfall. Heavy iron shutters seal the south and west doorways.

L3:cellar:A2.name: Raft Cellar
L3:cellar:A2.description: A ladder descends into a cramped brick basement of narrow ledges and dark gaps, cool and smelling of wet timber and pitch. Water drips somewhere unseen below. A stone shelf sits in the gloom at the end of the ledges, and the ladder leads back up to the chamber above.

L4:A1.name: Dripping Roost
L4:A1.description: A cramped chamber of damp blue stone opens off the entry hall to the east. Bat droppings streak the floor beneath cracks in the ceiling, and the steady drip of lake water echoes from somewhere overhead. The air is thick with mildew and the sour reek of guano.

L4:B1.name: Mouth of the Snake
L4:B1.description: The entry hall of the Snake lies beneath its lake island, walls of glistening blue-green brick carved with coiling serpents. Cold, wet air breathes up from the depths to the north, and a low side opening leads west. Behind, the stair climbs back toward daylight and the lap of lake water on the shore.

L4:B2.name: Moat Crossing
L4:B2.description: A channel of dark, still water cuts across this hall, crossed by a raised strip of flagstones. Long gouges near the doorways suggest something heavy and armored paces here. A locked door with a brass keyhole is set in the east wall, while open ways lead north and south.

L4:C2.name: Serpent Coil Chamber
L4:C2.description: Blocks are laid across the floor in a slow spiral, like the coils of a great snake turning toward the center of the room. Talon scratches mark the upper walls where winged things cling. The only way out is the locked door in the west wall, its keyhole furred with green corrosion.

L4:A3.name: Lane of Blocks
L4:A3.description: Two rows of squat stone blocks march down the length of this chamber, leaving a narrow lane between them. The vaulted ceiling is cracked and stained by seepage, and dark claw marks score the plaster near its peak. Openings lead east and north.

L4:B3.name: Seeping Gallery
L4:B3.description: Water oozes from the mortar in long green stains and gathers in shallow hollows across the floor. Fluttering echoes and a litter of droppings betray a roost in the dark vault above. The way out lies south, with a second opening to the west.

L4:A4.name: Still Corridor
L4:A4.description: A long, hushed hall lies quiet but for the sound of water moving behind its walls. Carved snake heads jut from each corner, their stone tongues worn smooth by centuries of damp. Puddles on the floor ripple faintly whenever the lake shifts. Passages open north and south.

L4:A5.name: Crackling Antechamber
L4:A5.description: Faint blue sparks crackle and fade in the air of this chamber, leaving a sharp tang like an oncoming storm. The bare floor is ringed by a border of raised blocks. To the north a locked door bars the way, its keyhole crusted with verdigris, and an open way leads south.

L4:B5.name: Hall of Biting Serpents
L4:B5.description: Wide flagstones stretch between walls carved with scaled serpents swallowing their own tails. A heavy iron shutter fills the east doorway, and to the north a door is fastened with a stout lock. Fresh scratches on the lintels hint at clawed things that perch above the doors.

L4:C5.name: Room of the Sunken Block
L4:C5.description: A broad moat of black water rings the middle of this chamber, and on the island it encloses one block sits a hair out of line with its fellows. Patches of sticky, glistening residue stain the flagstones near the water. The only door, a heavy shutter, lies to the west.

L4:A6.name: Divided Hall
L4:A6.description: Rows of blocks split this chamber into narrow lanes running north to south. A shutter of banded iron blocks the north door and a locked door guards the south, while the east side stands open. Torn scraps of leathery wing membrane lie scattered beneath the ledges.

L4:B6.name: Slick Chamber
L4:B6.description: Blobs of jelly-like slime glisten in the cracks between the flagstones, and the air carries a faintly sour smell. The north wall is crazed with hairline cracks around one thin, weak-looking section. A locked door stands to the south and an open way leads west.

L4:A7.name: Cold Crossing
L4:A7.description: This bare chamber is hushed and cold, its floor broken only by a lone column of blocks. Shutters seal the north and south doorways, and the eastern wall shows a patch of crumbling, discolored brick. Water trickles unseen somewhere beneath the floor.

L4:B7.name: The Sealed Heart
L4:B7.description: A small chamber lies walled in on every side, with no proper door at all. Yet each of the four walls bears a scarred, crumbling patch where the masonry looks thin and badly set. Grit sifts from the cracks whenever the lake presses against the foundations, and the air is stale.

L4:C7.name: Knight's Approach
L4:C7.description: Polished floor tiles are scored with long scrapes, as if armored feet drag across them on patrol. A massive shutter fills the east doorway, and a hiss and a reek of sulfur seep around its edges. The west wall is cracked and weak, and an open way leads north.

L4:D7.name: Gleeok's Lair
L4:D7.description: A vast hall of scorched stone opens beneath a ceiling blackened by fire. Twin fans of soot spread from the north wall where long serpent necks have reared and lashed, and cinders crunch underfoot. The air shimmers with heat and stinks of brimstone. Shutters close the north and west doors.

L4:A8.name: Hall of Twin Fires
L4:A8.description: Two fires burn in stone braziers at the far end of this chamber, their light dancing on walls slick with lake damp. Between them is a worn patch where an old man stands and speaks of a waterfall that hides more than water. The only door, a shutter, lies south.

L4:B8.name: Rafter Roost
L4:B8.description: Rotting timber rafters cross the low ceiling of this narrow room, and droppings crust the floor beneath them. The south wall sags around a breach of loose, crumbling brick that looks ready to give. To the east an open doorway leads on.

L4:C8.name: Gauntlet of Blades
L4:C8.description: Square recesses sit in the corners of this chamber, and deep grooves run from them along the walls and across the floor where something sharp and heavy slides at speed. The stone is chipped bright along those tracks. Open doorways lead west and south.

L4:D8.name: Triforce Chamber
L4:D8.description: A small sanctum of pale stone glows with a warm golden light that seems to rise from the floor itself. The endless drip of the lake falls silent here, and the carved serpents on the walls bow their heads toward the center. A shutter leads back south to the scorched lair.

L4:cellar:C5.name: Stepladder Cellar
L4:cellar:C5.description: A ladder drops from beneath the sunken block into a cramped basement of red brick. Narrow brick ledges step across a dark floor where water gurgles in the gaps, and the low ceiling sweats with lake seepage. The only way out is back up the ladder.

L5:C1.name: Lizard's Gate
L5:C1.description: The entry hall of the Lizard lies deep beneath the Lost Hills, its gray stone pillars carved with long-tailed lizards climbing toward the ceiling. The air is dry and dusty and tastes of old tombs. Doorways open north and east, and the stair behind climbs back to the windswept hills.

L5:D1.name: Echoing Chamber
L5:D1.description: Sound behaves strangely here: footsteps return from the walls doubled and distorted, and even a whisper hums back. Small round prints pock the dust as though something hops about. The north wall is cracked and weak-looking, and the west way leads back to the gate.

L5:A2.name: Western Stairwell
L5:A2.description: A dim, close room at the western edge of the labyrinth, its floor glazed with dried trails of slime. In one corner a narrow stair plunges into darkness, running far beneath the halls toward the north. The east wall bears a sagging, crumbled patch of masonry.

L5:B2.name: Tomb of Wrappings
L5:B2.description: Stone biers line the walls of this chamber, and scraps of yellowed linen lie trampled across the floor. The air is heavy with the sweet, dusty smell of embalming resin. A shutter seals the north door, and both the east and west walls show cracked, weak patches.

L5:C2.name: Embalmers' Hall
L5:C2.description: Long stone tables stained dark with old oils stand in the middle of this cross-shaped hall. Strips of grave cloth trail from them across the floor in shuffling paths. A shutter guards the north, the west wall is cracked and thin, and open doors lead east and south.

L5:D2.name: Hall of the Warning
L5:D2.description: Two small fires flicker on either side of a worn stone patch near the wall, painting the gray brick orange. Here an old man warns that the master of this place hates a certain kind of sound. A cracked section of the south wall looks weak, and the west way stands open.

L5:B3.name: Slime-Glazed Vault
L5:B3.description: The floor of this chamber gleams with a thin glaze of green slime that pools around the blocks set in its corners. Every step makes a wet, sucking sound, and the walls drip with the same ooze. Heavy shutters stand in the east and south doorways.

L5:C3.name: Hall of Heavy Tracks
L5:C3.description: Deep three-toed tracks crush the dust of this broad hall, and the air carries a faint smell of smoke and scorched hide. Shutters guard the west and south doors and a locked door bars the north, its iron keyhole rimmed with soot. An open way leads east.

L5:D3.name: Gray Junction
L5:D3.description: Mineral water drips from a fissure in the ceiling and spreads across the floor in long, shining trails. A row of weathered blocks leans against the east wall, and a stone lizard grins down from above the north door. Open ways lead north and west.

L5:C4.name: Hushed Archive
L5:C4.description: This silent chamber is lined with niches holding crumbling clay tablets etched with lizard glyphs. Dust lies thick and undisturbed over everything, and the faint scent of old parchment hangs in the air. A locked door stands in the south wall and an open way leads east.

L5:D4.name: Shuffling Passage
L5:D4.description: A long vaulted passage runs between rows of blocks, with scraps of linen caught on their corners like flags. A cold draft moves through it smelling of the grave and of dry resin. Open doorways lead north, south and west.

L5:A5.name: Sealed Crypt
L5:A5.description: A low crypt lies at the bottom of the western halls, reached only from the north where a heavy shutter hangs. Sarcophagus lids lean against the walls, pried open from the inside, and dust and linen threads float in the still air.

L5:D5.name: Lizard Shrine
L5:D5.description: A carved lizard of green stone coils on a pedestal against the east wall of this small shrine, its eyes worn blank by time. Faint slime trails wander across the floor around it, glinting in the gloom. Doorways lead north and south.

L5:A6.name: Digdogger's Den
L5:A6.description: The floor of this chamber is churned and dented as if a great rolling bulk had bounced across it a thousand times. The walls are pocked with deep, curving dents, and a low throb hums through the stone. A locked door lies east, and shutters close the north and south.

L5:B6.name: Whispering Gallery
L5:B6.description: Curved walls of polished stone carry every sound around this gallery and back again, until a single footstep becomes a chorus. The north wall shows a web of fine cracks around one thin section. A locked door bars the west, and the east stands open.

L5:C6.name: Ossuary
L5:C6.description: Bones are stacked in neat niches from floor to ceiling, and a trodden path of linen scraps crosses between them. The air is cold and smells of dust and resin. A locked door with a heavy keyhole stands to the east, and the way west is open.

L5:D6.name: Bat-Haunted Tomb
L5:D6.description: Coffins of carved stone stand in two rows across this tomb, their lids spattered with bat droppings. The rustle of wings echoes from the shadowed ceiling, and torn wrappings trail from one cracked casket. A locked door stands in the west wall, and the south is open.

L5:A7.name: Triforce Chamber
L5:A7.description: A quiet sanctum of pale gray stone rests above the battered den, its walls carved with lizards that turn their heads toward the center of the room. A golden light gathers in the still air, warm after the cold of the tombs. A shutter leads back south.

L5:B7.name: Hidden Sage's Nook
L5:B7.description: Tucked behind a false wall, this narrow room is lit by twin fires burning in stone bowls. Between them an old man murmurs that secret power is said to be in the arrow. The only way out is the broken wall to the south, its rubble still heaped on the floor.

L5:C7.name: Rafter Hall
L5:C7.description: Rotting beams cross the ceiling of this hall, white with the droppings of the things that roost there. The east wall bulges around a cracked, weak-looking section of brick. To the north a locked door bars the way, and leathery wingbeats echo overhead.

L5:D7.name: Sage's Bargain Room
L5:D7.description: A pair of fires crackles in stone braziers on either side of a worn spot by the north wall, warming this hidden room. Here an old man offers, for a price, to let a traveler carry more bombs. The only exit is the broken wall to the west.

L5:B8.name: Room of the Scraped Block
L5:B8.description: A grid of stone blocks fills this cramped northwestern chamber, and one block near the middle shows fresh scrape marks at its base. Slime trails glisten in the lanes between the rows, and the air is close and dry. A locked door leads east, its keyhole crusted with dust.

L5:C8.name: Stair Landing
L5:C8.description: A bare stone landing where a narrow stair drops into the floor, running far to the southwest beneath the halls. Locked doors stand in the south and west walls, their keyholes cold and dark. The dust around the stair is scuffed by many feet.

L5:cellar:B8.name: Recorder Cellar
L5:cellar:B8.description: A ladder descends beneath the scraped block into a narrow brick basement, where the dry air carries a faint, high whistle like wind across a reed. Brick ledges step across the dark floor, and the low ceiling presses close. The ladder is the only way back up.

L6:A1.name: Scorched Antechamber
L6:A1.description: Black scorch marks splash the walls of this chamber in starbursts, as if bolts of magic have struck them again and again. The smell of burnt air lingers. A locked door with a keyhole stands to the east, and the way north is open.

L6:B1.name: Dragon's Gate
L6:B1.description: Dragon statues of dark red stone flank the entry hall of this labyrinth, their jaws carved wide as if to breathe fire. Heat seems to radiate from the walls themselves. A locked door lies west and an open way leads east, and the stair behind climbs back to the open air.

L6:C1.name: Rune-Scored Hall
L6:C1.description: Arcane sigils are scratched across the flagstones here, and a few still glow faintly before fading. Soot blackens the corners and the air prickles against the skin. A locked door is set into the north wall, and an open way leads west.

L6:A2.name: Slime Cistern
L6:A2.description: Puddles of green slime pool in the low places of this sunken floor, and trails of it streak the walls up to knee height. A rusted drain grate in the center gurgles softly, breathing up a cold, sour draft. Open ways lead north and south.

L6:C2.name: Sour Cell
L6:C2.description: A small cell, reached only through a locked door in the south wall, holds nothing but a few squat blocks and a smear of slime along the floor. The walls close in, damp and red-tinged, and the air smells sour and stale. Nothing stirs here.

L6:A3.name: Smoky Roost
L6:A3.description: A tall, narrow chamber whose ceiling vanishes into soot-black shadow, alive with the rustle of leathery wings. Droppings crust the floor and the red stone walls. A heavy shutter seals the north door, and an open way leads south.

L6:A4.name: Blade Corridor
L6:A4.description: Grooves cut deep into the floor run from the corners toward the middle of this chamber, and the stone along them is nicked bright by something that slides at speed. The rest of the room is bare and quiet. Shutters guard both the north and south doors.

L6:A5.name: Flickering Hall
L6:A5.description: The air here crackles with stray sparks, and patches of the walls are scorched into strange silhouettes. Two rows of blocks run along the room, their tops blistered by heat. Heavy shutters close the north and south doorways.

L6:B5.name: Taloned Corner
L6:B5.description: Deep talon gouges mark the tops of the blocks set around this corner chamber, and torn wing membrane hangs from a crack in the ceiling. The red flagstones are cool underfoot. Heavy shutters stand in the north and east doorways.

L6:C5.name: Sorcerer's Stair
L6:C5.description: A spiral of scorch marks curls across the floor of this chamber toward its center. In the corner a narrow stair sinks into the floor, leading to distant halls far to the east. A shutter in the west wall is the only door.

L6:E5.name: Mage's Dead End
L6:E5.description: Burn marks of two colors, red-black and an eerie blue-gray, overlap on every wall of this isolated chamber. The air smells of ozone and singed stone, and the floor is gritty with ash. A shutter in the north wall is the only way out.

L6:A6.name: Statue Gallery
L6:A6.description: A line of dragon statues stands along the west wall, their stone faces blistered and cracked by stray spells. The east wall shows a crumbling patch of brick that looks thin. Heavy iron shutters close the north and south doors.

L6:B6.name: Ash Chamber
L6:B6.description: A drift of fine gray ash covers the floor, swirled into patterns by drafts that seem to come from nowhere. The west wall is cracked and weak, a shutter blocks the south, and a locked door with a scorched keyhole bars the north.

L6:E6.name: Threshold of the Nest
L6:E6.description: Grooves cut by sliding blades scar the floor, and blue scorch marks stain the walls of this hall. From behind the locked door in the north wall comes a dry rustle and the clatter of hard legs on stone. A shutter lies south and the east way is open.

L6:F6.name: Eastern Bend
L6:F6.description: This chamber at the eastern edge of the labyrinth smells of storm and singed fur. Sparks wink and vanish in the corners, and talon marks score the stone above the doorways. A cracked dragon carving leans in one corner. Open ways lead north and west.

L6:A7.name: Silent Vault
L6:A7.description: Bare red stone and a ring of blocks are all this chamber holds. No drafts stir here, and the hush is so complete that every footfall rings off the walls. Faint soot marks the lintels. Heavy shutters guard the east and south doors.

L6:B7.name: Hall of Many Doors
L6:B7.description: Four doorways meet in this crowded hall: locked doors to the north and south, a shutter to the west and an open way east. The floor is smeared with slime and a sticky, glistening film, and stray sparks snap in the corners. The walls are carved with coiling dragons.

L6:C7.name: Ember Hall
L6:C7.description: Glowing embers lie scattered in the cracks of this hall as though fire had rained from nowhere. The walls are scorched red-black in broad splashes, and the air is hot and dry. A shutter guards the north, and open ways lead east and west.

L6:D7.name: Northern Ascent
L6:D7.description: Low steps of red stone climb toward a shutter in the north wall, flanked by small dragon carvings with chipped snouts. Sparks crackle along the floor, and blue scorch marks streak the steps. An open way leads back west toward the ember-strewn hall.

L6:E7.name: Gohma's Nest
L6:E7.description: Shed carapace fragments and deep scuttle marks crisscross the floor of this lair, and the walls are gouged by great pincers. Above it all a single huge eye is carved into the north wall, staring and unblinking. Shutters close the north, and a locked door lies south.

L6:F7.name: Eastern Stairwell
L6:F7.description: A narrow stair sinks into the floor in one corner of this chamber, leading back toward the western halls. A sticky, glistening film coats the stones around it, and stray sparks snap in the air. The only door is the open way south.

L6:B8.name: Room of the Loose Block
L6:B8.description: Faint glyphs circle the floor of this northern chamber, and one of its blocks sits slightly askew, its base scraped bare of soot. Burn marks of red and blue overlap on the walls. A locked door lies south and the east wall looks cracked and weak.

L6:C8.name: Hall of Weak Walls
